plain: Money or a favor given to sway an official's act.

webster.text: A price, reward, gift or favor bestowed or promised with a view to pervert the judgment, or corrupt the conduct of a judge, witness or other person.

example.quote: Thus, in the old government, it is only necessary to bribe the few ; in the new government, it is necessary to corrupt the many.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, June 23, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
